title: Dark Nebula TGU H1674

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: An inky-black cloud blots out the stars in this view of the dark nebula TGU H1674, in the direction of Vela. Dark nebulae, also called absorption nebulae, are clouds of gas and dust so dense that they block visible light, leaving them black against the starry background.

The dust grains inside such clouds absorb and scatter the light of stars behind them. Dark nebulae are often cold and dense enough that new stars can form within them, hidden from view at visible wavelengths until they clear away their surroundings.

TGU H1674 is one of many objects found within a large 1.3-gigapixel image of the Vela Supernova Remnant. That image was captured with the Dark Energy Camera, which the Department of Energy fabricated, on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. Its filters isolate light from oxygen, from sulfur, and from hydrogen-alpha combined with nitrogen.
